chunks.document_title: NASA Spaceflight Medical Operations: Cardiovascular, Hypoxia, and Thermal Stabilization Summary
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA HRP Cardiovascular Adaptations and Spaceflight Medical Operations themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: Persistent resting tachycardia (heart rate elevated 20 to 40 bpm above personal baseline) and elevated arterial blood pressure (systolic >= 135 mmHg or diastolic >= 85 mmHg) during microgravity flight reflect autonomic baroreceptor unloading, vascular stiffness, and cephalad fluid redistribution. Crew members reporting palpitations, chest tightness, or vascular headache should suspend high-load resistive exercise, perform 10 minutes of paced vagal breathing, verify Astroskin ECG lead contact, and restrict dietary sodium below 2000 mg/day.

chunks.document_title: NASA Spaceflight Medical Operations: Cardiovascular, Hypoxia, and Thermal Stabilization Summary
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA HRP Cardiovascular Adaptations and Spaceflight Medical Operations themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: Arterial oxygen desaturation (SpO2 dropping below 95% warning or 90% critical) or core body temperature elevation (>= 37.8 C thermal strain) during EVA or habitat operations requires immediate verification of cabin oxygen partial pressure, supplemental oxygen mask administration if SpO2 is below 92%, workload reduction, liquid cooling garment flow adjustment, and 500 mL chilled oral electrolyte rehydration.

chunks.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Acute Radiation Syndromes Due to Solar Particle Events (Townsend et al., 2018)
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA HRP Acute Radiation Syndromes Evidence Report themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: During deep-space lunar and Mars transit outside Earth's magnetosphere, crew radiation dosimeters recording cumulative exposure above 1.5 mSv/day indicate elevated ionizing flux from a Solar Particle Event (SPE) or Galactic Cosmic Rays. Prodromal clinical symptoms include systemic fatigue, mild nausea, anorexia, oxidative stress, and elevated resting heart rate.

chunks.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Acute Radiation Syndromes Due to Solar Particle Events (Townsend et al., 2018)
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA HRP Acute Radiation Syndromes Evidence Report themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: Immediate operational countermeasures for elevated radiation dosimetry exceeding 1.5 mSv/day require relocating crew members to the spacecraft's high-mass polyethylene storm shelter zone until dosimeter rates fall below 0.5 mSv/day, accompanied by oral electrolyte hydration (1500 mL/day) and antioxidant-rich carotenoid spaceflight rations.

chunks.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) (Stenger et al., 2017)
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA Human Research Program (HRP) SANS Evidence Report themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: In- and post-flight changes in visual acuity and structural changes of the eye include unilateral or bilateral optic disc edema, globe flattening, choroidal folds, cotton wool spots, and hyperopic refractive error shift. Astronauts on long-duration microgravity missions frequently report progressive near-vision blurriness when reading instrument panels and mild retro-orbital pressure or headache caused by cephalad fluid shifts toward the head.

chunks.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) (Stenger et al., 2017)
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA Human Research Program (HRP) SANS Evidence Report themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: Mechanical and nutritional countermeasures investigated by the NASA Human Research Program to mitigate cephalad venous congestion in SANS include Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) sessions at -20 to -25 mmHg to sequester fluid in the lower extremities, restricting dietary sodium intake below 2000 mg per day, and supporting one-carbon metabolism pathway enzymes with folate and vitamin B12 nutritional supplementation.

chunks.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload (Flynn-Evans et al., 2016)
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA HRP Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization Evidence Report themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: Circadian desynchronization and sleep loss during spaceflight reduce total sleep time, degrade Actiwatch sleep quality scores below 60, and elevate prefrontal fNIRS cognitive fatigue indices above 0.65. Crew members experience daytime drowsiness, impaired psychomotor vigilance, mood irritability, and elevated sympathetic resting heart rate.

chunks.document_title: NASA HRP Evidence Report: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload (Flynn-Evans et al., 2016)
chunks.provenance: Paraphrased prototype summary based on NASA HRP Sleep Loss and Circadian Desynchronization Evidence Report themes. Not verbatim clinical guidance.
chunks.content: Countermeasure protocols to entrain circadian phase alignment in spacecraft habitats utilize the Solid-State Lighting Assembly (SSLA) set to 460nm blue-enriched high-melanopic spectrum for 30 minutes during the wake window, shifting to warm red-depleted lighting 90 minutes before sleep, eliminating caffeine 8 hours prior to sleep, and following Flight Surgeon pre-sleep circadian alignment protocols.
